chapter_title: Chương 67: 0067 【Trưởng phòng đào tạo Trần Quý Lương học hành tốt, luôn hiểu chuyện và vâng lời】

segments.title: Chương 67: 0067 【Trưởng phòng đào tạo Trần Quý Lương học hành tốt, luôn hiểu chuyện và vâng lời】
segments.content:
The 28th of the twelfth lunar month, noon.

"Ma'am, how do I get to No. 2 Middle School?"

"Keep going straight. After a few intersections, there's a roundabout. Pass the big roundabout and keep going forward. Ignore the intersections you see, and when you see a traffic light, turn left. Follow that road straight, and when you get to a street full of internet cafes, you can ask again."

"Thank you, Ma'am."

Reporter Chen Feng stepped on the gas. Six or seven minutes later, he arrived at the street of internet cafes.

Business here wasn't great. With the students all on vacation, there were no customers, so some internet cafes had simply closed for the holidays.

After asking for directions again and driving for another minute or two, he finally arrived at the school gate.

But the main gate was locked tight, and the shops outside the school were all closed for the holidays.

He had no choice but to get out of his car and wander around. After walking for several minutes, he finally ran into a living soul.

"Sir, I'm a reporter from the Xihua Metropolis Daily. Excuse me, how can I find the principal of No. 2 Middle School?"

"How should I know? Go that way, enter through the back gate of No. 2 Middle School. The faculty and staff residential area is inside."

"Thank you, Sir."

Chen Feng ran over to the school's back gate. His luck was pretty good; he managed to get the Dean of Studies' phone number directly from the security guard.

"Hello, Director Yang, this is Chen Feng, a reporter from the Xihua Metropolis Daily."

"Hello, Reporter Chen."

"I'm currently at the back gate of No. 2 Middle School. I'd like to interview one of the school leaders."

"Certainly, certainly. Please wait a moment, I'll be right over. May I ask what your newspaper wishes to learn about?"

"There's a student at No. 2 Middle School named Chen Guiliang who won first prize in the New Concept Composition Competition. And his essay is highly regarded; schools like Tsinghua, Peking, Fudan, and Beijing Normal University are all fighting to give him special admission."

"You're talking about Chen Guiliang?"

"Is there a problem with Chen Guiliang?"

"No, absolutely no problem. Student Chen Guiliang studies in our experimental class for the third year of high school. He has always been sensible and obedient, studies hard, gets along with his classmates, and excels in both character and academics. Reporter Chen, please wait a moment, I'll be there within ten minutes!"

The Dean of Studies, Yang Zhenzhong, didn't live in the faculty and staff residential area. He had bought a house in the new district last year.

He snatched up his worn-out car keys and went downstairs, calling the principal as he ran: "Principal Yan, great news!"

Principal Yan laughed and said, "What, are you calling to wish me an early New Year?"

"Where are you right now?" Yang Zhenzhong asked.

Principal Yan said, "I'm having a meal with a friend. It just so happens Guo Xiao Si is home for the New Year, so I asked this friend to invite him to come back to his alma mater next semester to give a lecture and make a donation. Then we can invite twenty or thirty media outlets for some publicity."

Next semester, Guo Xiao Si would indeed come.

He held a literature lecture, signed some books, and donated five thousand yuan to his alma mater.

But the travel expenses for the twenty or thirty media reporters cost a small fortune!

Fushi County was too remote, and the road conditions were extremely poor. Even for a reporter from Rongcheng, a trip here would take two days. If a reporter from Modu were to come, the arduous journey would take several days, and one or two thousand yuan would be nowhere near enough to cover it.

Yang Zhenzhong said, "Our school has produced another first-prize winner in the New Concept competition. It seems to be a big deal; Tsinghua, Peking, and Fudan are fighting for his special admission."

"Where did you hear this news?" Principal Yan asked, pleasantly surprised.

Yang Zhenzhong said, "A reporter from the Xihua Metropolis Daily is already here, waiting at the school's back gate."

Principal Yan said, "Then you go receive him immediately. You must keep him there. I'm in the city center; it'll take me at least forty minutes to get there."

"Okay, I'm on my way to my car."

Yang Zhenzhong hung up the phone and then called Chen Guiliang's homeroom teacher.

"Teacher Liu, where are you?"

"Visiting relatives."

"Is it far?"

"Huangge Town."

"Have your husband drive you back to the school's back gate right away."

Liu Shuying was completely baffled. She said to her husband, "Drive back to the school."

"We're leaving without finishing the meal?" said Gao Zhan.

The couple had gone to her parents' home for an early reunion dinner today. They would spend New Year's Eve at their own home, and then visit Gao Zhan's parents on the second day of the New Year.

Liu Shuying said, "It's an emergency. Just drive."

Gao Zhan could only grumble as he walked toward his Chery QQ.

Liu Shuying then gave a simple explanation to her relatives.

Their daughter, who was in university, was also home for winter break. She chased after them and asked, "Even if it's an emergency, you should at least finish eating before you go."

"Don't worry about it."

On the way back to the county town, Gao Zhan asked, "What on earth is going on?"

"I don't know," Liu Shuying said.

Gao Zhan had gotten his car two months ago and had already honed his driving skills. He was driving the Chery QQ like a race car.

Rushing as fast as they could, they arrived at the school's back gate. Just as they got out of the car, someone came up to greet them: "Teacher Gao, Teacher Liu, sorry to interrupt your meal. I'm Chen Feng, a reporter from the Xihua Metropolis Daily."

"Hello, Reporter Chen!"

The couple quickly shook his hand.

Yang Zhenzhong explained, "Here's the situation. Your student, that outstanding Chen Guiliang from your class, wrote an excellent essay for the New Concept Composition Competition this time. Tsinghua and Peking University are both fighting to have him. Because it was written so well, the supplementary editor of Wen Wei Po was highly suspicious and gave him a topic on the spot, asking him to write a classical poem. And the result? Student Chen Guiliang lived up to everyone's expectations and produced a modern-day version of 'composing a poem in seven steps.'"

Liu Shuying thought to herself: You were the one who personally signed off on Chen Guiliang's 'probationary discipline,' and now you're calling him outstanding in character and academics?

Gao Zhan was stunned at first, but then he reacted quickly: "Chen Guiliang is a student I've always liked very much. I knew long ago that he was exceptionally talented. In his second year of high school, he brought a copy of the *Critique of Pure Reason* and came to ask me how he should understand it. Just a second-year student, and he was already reading Kant's books."

This was a true story. At the time, Gao Zhan had been unable to answer and had told Chen Guiliang to read less miscellaneous books.

Without a good teacher to clear up his confusion, Chen Guiliang could only read blindly.

"He was reading Kant in his second year?" Chen Feng was quite surprised, taking out his notepad to jot it down.

Gao Zhan said, "He reads all kinds of books..."

Just as he was speaking, a taxi pulled up to the side of the road, and the Chinese teacher, Li Runze, also arrived.

"Reporter Chen, this is Chen Guiliang's Chinese teacher," Yang Zhenzhong quickly introduced.

After shaking hands and greeting each other, Chen Feng explained the purpose of his visit.

Yang Zhenzhong said, "Now that everyone's here, why don't we go eat first? I already booked a table at a restaurant on my way here."

Ten minutes later, the group arrived at a private room in the restaurant.

Li Runze was still carrying a thermos. He took a sip of goji berry tea and said with considerable pride, "Chen Guiliang is my Chinese class representative. I've been teaching him since his first year. After every exam, I would always use his essay as a model to explain to the other students. From his first to his third year, he got a perfect score on his essays twice and never scored below 56."

Chen Feng scribbled furiously in his notepad, "Has he shown any aptitude for classical Chinese before?"

"Yes," Li Runze said, "He started writing classical poetry in his second year and even asked me to buy him a copy of Mr. Wang Li's *Chinese Poetic Prosody*. You can't find this book in the Xinhua Bookstore; he heard about the title online. I had to call an old friend in Yangcheng to mail me a used copy."

Chen Feng continued taking notes, "As his Chinese teacher, it seems you've helped him a great deal."

Li Runze took another sip of his goji berry tea, "When you encounter a promising student, of course you have to nurture them. Before we managed to buy *Chinese Poetic Prosody*, guess how Chen Guiliang studied poetry and classical Chinese?"

"How?" Chen Feng asked.

Yang Zhenzhong passed two cigarettes to the side, then went out to hurry the waitress with their food.

Li Runze smiled and said, "He recited the *Three Hundred Tang and Song Poems* on one hand, and the *Dictionary of Ancient Chinese* on the other."

"He even recited the *Dictionary of Ancient Chinese*?" Chen Feng asked in astonishment.

Li Runze said, "Yes. I was also very surprised at the time, so I asked him why he was memorizing a dictionary. He said it was a habit he formed as a child. He went to a village primary school, where one teacher taught all subjects for all grades. That teacher was a community-run teacher, earning only a few yuan a month, and had to take the public teacher qualification exam every year. Whenever he was preparing for the exam, that teacher wouldn't lecture; he'd just have the students memorize their textbooks. Chen Guiliang said he memorized all of his primary school textbooks."

"That is interesting," Chen Feng said with a smile.

Li Runze said, "He developed a habit after that. When he really had nothing else to read, he even memorized the *Xinhua Dictionary*. A kid from the countryside, where would he find extracurricular books to read?"

Chen Feng sighed with emotion, "That's not easy at all."

Li Runze said, "He also brought *Zhuangzi* to ask me questions. Not about the meaning of words, but about Zhuangzi's philosophy. How could I possibly answer that? We could only discuss it together. This kid, I've also seen him reading *Laozi*, *Huainanzi*, and *General Treatise on the Zhou Yi*. Anyway, none of them are books that someone his age should be reading."

It really took a Chinese teacher for this, Chen Feng felt he had made the right decision coming for this interview.

Li Runze continued, "Chen Guiliang used to be very thin. His family is poor, and he loves to read, so he'd skip breakfast and avoid meat dishes to save money to buy extracurricular books. It's only recently, probably because he's in the final push for the Gaokao, that he started eating properly."

Liu Shuying listened in a daze.

She thought she was very caring and knew her students well, but she had no idea about any of this.

The dishes were finally served, and Yang Zhenzhong produced a bottle of Wuliangye.

"Reporter Chen, let's eat and talk," Yang Zhenzhong said as he helped pour the liquor.

Chen Feng held up his hand to stop him, "You're too kind. I still have to drive back to Rongcheng, so I won't drink. The road conditions are bad, and I'm afraid of an accident."

"The road is indeed difficult, I've driven it myself. Some sections of the provincial highway are worse than village roads, they can shake the bones right out of you," Yang Zhenzhong said, agreeing with him.

After a few bites of food, Chen Feng asked Liu Shuying, "How are Chen Guiliang's academic results usually?"

Liu Shuying said, "His high school entrance exam scores were excellent, he only lost a dozen or so points, and he was in the experimental class in his first year. During the placement exams, he scored over 90 in math, physics, and chemistry. Perhaps it was his love for literature, but he insisted on joining the liberal arts track. As you've just heard, Reporter Chen, he devotes all his energy to reading extracurricular books. His grades in his second and third years have slipped a bit; he can only hover around the cut-off line for first-tier universities."

In fact, most of the time he was below the first-tier cut-off; only on rare occasions when he performed exceptionally well could he reach it.

After a few more bites, Chen Feng asked, "Does he have any interesting anecdotes from school?"

Yang Zhenzhong frantically winked at Liu Shuying.

What interesting anecdotes?

Putting up a big-character poster criticizing the principal? Or smearing the cafeteria's spoiled food, liquid and all, on the principal's office door?

Or maybe leading a protest in the cafeteria and smashing all the bowls and plates?

Or how about in the third year, when the school collected computer fees but didn't hold computer classes, he organized students to sign a petition demanding a refund?

Liu Shuying racked her brain, searching her memory carefully, and finally thought of something she could mention, "In his second year, a third-year student got leukemia. The school organized a donation drive, and Chen Guiliang donated twenty yuan. His donation ranked second in the entire class."

Chen Feng didn't know whether to laugh or cry. What was there to say about something like that?

But then he connected it to Chen Guiliang going hungry to buy books, and it seemed perhaps worthy of some praise.

"Are there any of those peculiar or extraordinary stories?" Chen Feng continued to ask.

"No," Liu Shuying shook her head.

Chen Feng thought to himself: Looks like I'll have to go interview Chen Guiliang's junior high teachers.

(When I, Lao Wang, was in elementary school, I really did memorize the entire Chinese textbook. The teacher was an old lady in her 50s who still had to review materials for the public teacher exam at her age. She wouldn't teach for days on end but required students to stay in the classroom and memorize their books...)
